title: What Students Want, According to a Survey
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Stuart reflects on a 100-student Study.com survey about what students want from their teachers, interpreting each finding through the lens of his Five Key Beliefs framework. He maps passionate teaching to Credibility, teacher influence on liking a subject to Value, emotional support to MGCs, personalized explanations to both Credibility and Effort belief cultivation, and student recognition of teacher effort to the broader case for focusing work on what matters most. The piece is a motivating validation: students want and notice precisely the things the Five Key Beliefs framework prioritizes, and they want to want to learn—which reframes student motivation as a shared goal between teacher and student rather than a problem the teacher imposes solutions upon.
points: 82% of students feel more encouraged to learn when their teacher is passionate about the subject, confirming that passion is a demonstrable component of Teacher Credibility—and one that can be expressed through Gentle Urgency rather than overt enthusiasm.

72% of students said a teacher helped them enjoy a subject they didn’t expect to like, providing direct survey evidence that teacher behavior substantially shapes student perceptions of subject value.

90% of students said having a teacher who cares about their emotional well-being helps them perform better in school—a direct endorsement of MGCs and care-conscious instructional design as academically consequential, not merely relational.
92% of students said they notice how hard their teacher works, meaning teacher effort is visible and influential and reinforces the case for focusing that effort on the highest-leverage activities.

The survey’s most encouraging implication: students want what teachers want—enjoyable and productive learning experiences—positioning student motivation not as resistance to overcome but as an appetite to cultivate.
quotes: 82% of students felt more encouraged to learn when their teacher is passionate about the subject.
Passion is part of the CCP of Credibility. Thankfully, passion can be demonstrated by more than just over-the-top enthusiasm (my personality doesn’t tend toward much of that).
72% of students said a teacher helped them enjoy a subject they didn’t expect to like or thought they weren’t good at. This is the language of Value.
90% of students said having a teacher who cares about their emotional well-being helps them do better in school.
92% of students said they notice the hard work teachers put into their work. I love this. Almost every student surveyed said they can see the work we put in.
students want what we want: enjoyable and productive learning experiences. They WANT us to succeed. They WANT to WANT to learn.
